Definition: a provincial form of the derivative of the base of G2962; a "tyrant"; Tyrannus, an Ephesian:--Tyrannus.
BiblicalUsage: Tyrannus is the man of Ephesus in whose school Paul taught for two years. In Acts 19:9, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Tyrannus shows me God keeps His promises across generations, even through flawed families.
